Mission Local’s four takeaways were:

- Turnout was 78.9%: above the city’s 77% average for presidential elections, but well below 2020’s 86.3%. About 412,000 people voted, roughly 38,000 fewer than in 2020, despite a similar number of registered voters.
- Geography shaped results. Proposition K passed citywide 55–45, but voters in districts near the Great Highway opposed it; supervisor races also showed neighborhood-level divides.
- Campaigns spent at least $72 million. The article said campaigns focused more on persuading voters—especially through advertising—than on getting them to the polls. Daniel Lurie’s mayoral campaign was the most expensive, at about $16 million.
- Redistricting affected several supervisor races: the article described likely effects in Districts 5 and 7, as well as new precincts’ impact on races in Districts 1 and 3.

The article’s correction says an earlier version misstated the number of registered voters. It does not provide the corrected figure in the correction note.
